A1.justification: Both complete, readable 30-page PDFs describe the same theoretical work. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover Table 1, equations, references, and Appendices A–C without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports mathematical definitions, evaluability guarantees, and proofs, including constructed distributions in Appendices A–C. It contains no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v3 likewise contains theoretical results and proofs without original empirical outcomes. Empirical studies mentioned in the paper are cited prior work.

M1.justification: The evaluation algorithms and score functions, including IPM-based comparisons and negative-log-likelihood scoring, are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets for empirical training or evaluation. The illustrative applications and theoretical distribution constructions are unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline comparisons. The algorithms and theoretical comparisons discussed in relation to prior density-estimation work are retained.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols, data splits, training budgets, or testing procedures are added or revised. The theoretical sampling setup remains identical.

E4.justification: The analytical counterexamples and proof constructions are identical. Neither version reports empirical ablations, robustness tests, or case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run statistics, seeds, or uncertainty estimates. The theoretical confidence parameters and concentration bounds are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains every evaluability guarantee, and all analytical bounds and findings remain unchanged. Its coverage-profile citation changes year, but no result changes.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions, theorem statements, sample-complexity bounds, and derivations are unchanged. Appendices A–C are identical in extracted text and rendered appearance.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions concerning evaluability, IPMs, Rényi/KL divergences, and perplexity. No scientific claim is strengthened, narrowed, or added.

C2.justification: The explanations involving rare events, coverage-threshold discontinuity, and perplexity's geometric mismatch are unchanged, as are applicability assumptions and the open questions in Section 6.

D1.justification: No implementation instructions, hyperparameters, computational resources, or code/data access information are added or revised. The additional publication metadata concerns references.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Chen et al., Huang et al., and van Erven and Harremoës receive updated years and publication details, but remain the same cited works.

P1.justification: v3 updates citation years, expands bibliographic metadata, and edits reference capitalization and author formatting, alongside the version/date stamp. The scientific exposition and section structure are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded references reflow across pages 15–16, moving the Martins, Müller, and Pillutla entries onto page 16. Table 1 retains its layout, and the scientific pages and appendices retain their visual organization.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies publication venues and page information for previously sparse references, including Djolonga et al. and Martins et al., and updates preprint entries to publication records. This modestly improves bibliographic completeness and reference identification. The scientific arguments, findings, and proofs are unchanged.
